title: I've been using frontier AI models to create reusable 2D character rigs and generate endless character variations with them
author: Crockiestar
selftext:
I've been working on an animation software called **Warp Studio,** and I wanted to share a pretty interesting workflow I've discovered with its 2D character animation tool, Warp Puppet.

Warp Puppet uses a mesh deformation system that lets you rig and animate 2D characters by placing and moving pins around, without needing to manually redraw frames. The software also has full **MCP support**, meaning you can connect frontier models like ChatGPT Codex, Claude, or Gemini and have them directly operate the animation tools to help rig and animate your characters.

One of the more interesting workflows I've been experimenting with involves creating **reusable character rigs that can support countless different character designs.**

Instead of having an image generation model create a finished character, I get a frontier coding model to **draw the character from scratch using math**, separating the design into individual movable body parts and arranging everything onto a parts sheet. This gives you much more control over the exact shapes, proportions, and placement of each component.

I can then bring that sheet into Warp Puppet and have the AI help rig it using the mesh deformation tools.

Once you have a character's movable parts arranged on a sheet, you can use image generation models like ChatGPT's image generator or Google's Imagen to **completely redesign the character while preserving the arrangement of its individual parts.**

That means you can turn one character into all kinds of different creatures, outfits, or character designs that can reuse the same rig and animations. You can also mix and match individual parts between compatible designs.

Check it out here: [Warp Studio](https://crockiestar.itch.io/warp-studio)
